title: Root Dockerfile runs container as root (no USER directive)
description: The root Dockerfile defines three build stages (builder, builder-two, runner) but never declares a USER directive, so the final runner image and its entrypoint execute with UID 0 (root). A container escape or RCE in the Node process therefore runs with root privileges inside the container. Best practice is to add a non-root USER in the runner stage (CWE-250 execution with unnecessary privileges).
evidence: FROM node:20 AS runner ... CMD ['/calcom/scripts/start.sh'] (no USER directive in any of the 3 stages)

title: API v2 Dockerfile runs container as root (no USER directive)
description: The api-v2 Dockerfile (FROM node:20-alpine) exposes port 80 and launches the NestJS process via CMD without ever declaring a USER, so the API server runs as root. Add a dedicated non-root user before the CMD to reduce the blast radius of a compromise (CWE-250/CWE-269).

title: GitHub Action pinned to mutable tag instead of commit SHA
description: The security-audit workflow references actions/checkout@v4, a mutable tag that a compromised or re-tagged upstream release could repoint to malicious code executed inside CI with repository credentials. This unpinned-action pattern generalizes across the repository's 59 workflow files. Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA (CWE-1357 reliance on insufficiently trustworthy component).

title: Default hardcoded auth/encryption secrets in Dockerfile build args
description: The root Dockerfile defaults two security-critical build args to the literal string secret: ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret (L11) and ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret (L12), and both are baked into ENV (L29-30). If an image is built without explicitly overriding these args, session signing (NEXTAUTH_SECRET) and at-rest encryption (CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) use a trivially guessable key, enabling session forgery and decryption of stored credentials (CWE-798 use of hardcoded credentials).

title: Concrete hardcoded CRON_API_KEY committed in .env template
description: The committed environment template contains a realistic 32-hex-character secret value for CRON_API_KEY rather than an empty placeholder. Operators who copy .env.example to .env verbatim will ship a publicly known cron API key that authenticates privileged cron endpoints, allowing unauthorized job invocation (CWE-798 use of hardcoded credentials).

title: Wildcard CORS origin permitted in non-production only
description: enableCors() resolves its origin to the wildcard * as the final fallback, but only when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset AND NODE_ENV is not production (production defaults to false, i.e. CORS disabled). The wildcard is therefore confined to local/dev convenience and does not weaken production, so severity is low; operators should still set ALLOWED_ORIGINS explicitly (CWE-942 permissive cross-domain policy).

title: CSP script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' (prod fallback) and 'unsafe-eval' (dev)
description: getCspPolicy() emits a production script-src containing 'unsafe-inline' https: (alongside a per-request nonce and 'strict-dynamic') and a development script-src containing 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https: http:. The unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval tokens weaken XSS protection; they are a documented browser-compat fallback and are partially neutralized by 'strict-dynamic' in supporting browsers. Strong compensating controls exist (nonce, strict-dynamic, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none'), so severity is medium (CWE-1021/CWE-79).

title: Global static CSP header allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' scripts
description: The Next.js headers() config sets a static Content-Security-Policy for source /:path* whose script-src permits 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https:. Unlike the nonce-based edge CSP, this header applies to all matched routes in every environment and permits inline script and eval(), materially weakening XSS defense. Compensating directives (frame-ancestors 'self', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self') limit but do not remove the risk (CWE-79).

title: API v1 accepts API key via URL query string
description: The v1 API middleware reads the caller's API key from req.query.apiKey. Secrets placed in URLs can leak through server/proxy access logs, browser history, and Referer headers (CWE-598 use of GET request with sensitive query strings). Risk is reduced because the key is immediately hashed via hashAPIKey() before any DB lookup and the modern v2 strategy uses a Bearer Authorization header plus sha256Hash, so severity is low.

title: Default Postgres service credentials in docker-compose
description: The database service hardcodes default credentials POSTGRES_USER=unicorn_user (L20) and POSTGRES_PASSWORD=magical_password (L21). These well-known defaults would grant DB access to anyone who can reach the service. Exposure is limited because the database service publishes no host port and lives on the internal stack network (external: false); however the optional Prisma Studio service exposes port 5555 with only a documented prod-removal warning (L120). Operators must override these before any non-local deployment (CWE-798/CWE-1188).

title: npm audit advisory 1113407 suppressed for fast-xml-parser
description: npmAuditIgnoreAdvisories suppresses advisory 1113407 (fast-xml-parser 4.4.1, transitive via @boxyhq/saml-jackson -> @aws-sdk/core). The suppression is documented and justified in-file (L7-9): the parser only handles trusted AWS API responses (not user input) and an upstream fix is pending release. This is an accepted, documented risk (mitigation_present) rather than an unmanaged one, hence low/informational; it must be correlated with the Layer 4 SCA result during cross-layer merge (D8).
